name: Matthias Mason & Co.'s Blacksmith Shop

documented_range.note: SELF-REPORTED IN THE ONLY CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO DOCUMENT THIS PROJECT HOLDS. Mason & Co. advertise as blacksmiths in the Chicago Democrat of 26 November 1833, on 'Main-street, nearly opposite Graves' Tavern'. The '& Co.' says the shop employed more than one man. The far end of the range is inferred: nothing follows the firm past 1833, and a working smithy in a town growing tenfold is far more likely to have continued than to have closed.

position.symbolic_location: South Division, local ENU E 735 N -133
position.note: THE ADDRESS IS DOCUMENTED IN A STREET NAME NOBODY ELSE USES, AND THE CROSS-REFERENCE IS WHAT PLACES IT. 'Main-street' appears nowhere in data/traces/street_control.json, the Thompson plat module or either 1834 sheet. Graves' Tavern is Dexter Graves's log tavern, which this dataset models as mansion_house at what became 84-86 Lake Street, on the NORTH side of Lake near Dearborn. 'Nearly opposite' therefore puts the smithy on the SOUTH side of Lake Street facing north across it, and 'Main-street' in November 1833 is very probably Lake Street under a colloquial name. The northing is the Lake Street south frontage band this dataset's reconstruction recipes already use; the easting is set opposite mansion_house. WHAT IS INVENTED: the exact lot, the setback and the facade bearing.

derivation.reason: No source gives this building a lot. The placement is a frontage-band assignment tested for clearance and buildable ground, which is a production control and not a derivation from any line in the dataset.

footprint.note: PLACEHOLDER - NO DIMENSION IS ATTESTED. 20 x 30 ft is a two-fire shop: room for two hearths, an anvil each and a horse standing in, which is what '& Co.' implies. Every number is invented.
